name: British Columbia Provincial Police Force
description: Established in 1871 as the British Columbia Constabulary, the provincial police came under the Attorney-General's authority at Confederation and existed until 1950.

name: Workmen's Compensation Board
description: Established 1 January 1917 under the Workmen's Compensation Act; renamed by proclamation on 1 July 1974.

name: Workers' Compensation Board of British Columbia
description: Statutory workers' compensation and workplace-safety agency, renamed from the Workmen's Compensation Board in 1974 and operating as WorkSafeBC.

name: Civil Service Commission
description: Established under the Civil Service Act of 1917 to administer testing for admission and promotion in the civil service; renamed the Public Service Commission by the Public Service Act of 1973.

name: Pacific Great Eastern Railway Company
description: Railway incorporated privately on 27 February 1912 and taken over by the provincial government in 1918 after its contractors withdrew; renamed the British Columbia Railway Company on 1 April 1972.

name: Game Conservation Board
description: Board established April 1918 to administer the Game Act; abolished in 1929 and replaced by a Game Commissioner.

name: Provincial Game Commissioner
description: Single commissioner responsible for game administration and enforcement, replaced by the Game Commission in 1934.

name: Game Commission
description: Commission established in 1934 and constituted by statute in 1935, replacing the Provincial Game Commissioner.

name: Public Library Commission
description: Created by the Public Libraries Act of 1919, administered by the Provincial Secretary, to fund and support public library associations and travelling libraries.

name: Liquor Control Board
description: Established under the Government Liquor Act of 1921, which repealed Prohibition, to run government liquor stores and issue permits; dissolved in 1973 and its functions split between the Liquor Administration Branch and the BC Liquor Board.

name: Liquor Distribution Branch
description: Government branch that took over the Liquor Control Board's store operations in 1973 (first as the Liquor Administration Branch) and now runs BC Liquor and BC Cannabis Stores.

name: Coal and Petroleum Control Board
description: Board created in 1937 to license and regulate the coal and petroleum industries; most of its mandate passed to the Public Utilities Commission in 1951 and it was disestablished in 1953.

name: Public Utilities Commission
description: Quasi-judicial regulator of utility rates and service created by the Public Utilities Act of 1938 (an earlier 1919 commission had been short-lived); terminated in 1973, with its energy functions passing to the BC Energy Commission.

name: Labour Relations Board
description: Board created under the Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act of 1947 to certify bargaining units and resolve disputes; made independent under the 1973 Labour Code and renamed the Industrial Relations Council in 1987.

name: Industrial Relations Council
description: Name given to the Labour Relations Board by the Industrial Relations Reform Act of 1987, reversed by the Labour Relations Code of 1992.

name: Labour Relations Board
description: Labour tribunal restored under its former name by the Labour Relations Code of 1992.

name: British Columbia Power Commission
description: Public utility created by the Hart government to electrify areas not served by BC Electric; amalgamated with the nationalized BC Electric Company on 31 March 1962 to form BC Hydro.

name: British Columbia Hospital Insurance Service

responsible.ministry: Dept. of Health Services and Hospital Insurance

description: Branch established in 1949 under the Hospital Insurance Act of 1948 to run provincial hospital insurance; renamed Hospital Programs in 1975.

name: British Columbia Toll Highways and Bridges Authority
description: Crown authority established 2 December 1953 whose ferry division began the government ferry service in 1960; renamed the British Columbia Ferry Authority on 1 April 1964.

name: British Columbia Ferry Authority
description: Crown ferry operator renamed from the Toll Highways and Bridges Authority in 1964 and renamed the British Columbia Ferry Corporation on 1 January 1977.

name: British Columbia Ferry Corporation
description: Crown corporation established under the British Columbia Ferry Corporation Act effective 1 January 1977; converted on 2 April 2003 into an independent regulated company, British Columbia Ferry Services Inc.

name: British Columbia Ferry Services Inc.
description: Former Crown corporation converted in 2003 under the Coastal Ferry Act into an independently managed, publicly owned company whose single voting share is held by the provincial B.C. Ferry Authority (not a Crown corporation).

name: Capital Improvement District Commission
description: Commission created by statute on 1 March 1956 to fund improvement and beautification projects in the Victoria capital region; became the Provincial Capital Commission in 1977.

name: British Columbia Electric Company (provincially owned)
description: The private BC Electric utility, expropriated by the provincial government on 1 August 1961 and merged with the BC Power Commission in 1962 to form BC Hydro.

name: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority
description: Provincial electric utility formed by merging the nationalized BC Electric Company with the BC Power Commission; it shed its gas and transit operations from 1979 and re-absorbed BC Transmission Corporation in 2010.

name: British Columbia Housing Management Commission
description: Constituted a body corporate by order in council approved 8 December 1967 to develop, administer and manage social housing; known as BC Housing.

name: Mediation Commission
description: Commission established under the Mediation Commission Act to mediate labour disputes; its functions passed to the Department of Labour's Mediation Services Branch in 1972.

name: British Columbia Railway Company
description: Renamed from the Pacific Great Eastern Railway in 1972 and operated as BC Rail from 1984; its freight operations were leased to CN in 2004, and it continues to hold railway and port lands as a subsidiary of the BC Transportation Financing Authority.

name: British Columbia Development Corporation
description: Crown corporation established 31 March 1973 to assist industrial enterprises; merged into the new British Columbia Enterprise Corporation effective 31 March 1987.

name: British Columbia Energy Commission
description: Established under the Energy Act of 1973 to take over the energy functions of the Public Utilities Commission; replaced by the British Columbia Utilities Commission in 1980.

name: Insurance Corporation of British Columbia
description: Crown corporation created in 1973 by the Barrett government to administer compulsory public auto insurance (Autoplan) and later driver and vehicle licensing.

name: British Columbia Land Commission
description: Created by the Land Commission Act, proclaimed 18 May 1973, which also established the Agricultural Land Reserve.

name: Provincial Agricultural Land Commission
description: The Land Commission renamed under the Agricultural Land Commission Act of January 1978; it administers the Agricultural Land Reserve.

name: Ocean Falls Corporation
description: Formed in 1973 when the province bought the town of Ocean Falls and its pulp mill from Crown Zellerbach; the mill closed in 1980 and the corporation was dissolved in 1986.

name: British Columbia Petroleum Corporation
description: Crown corporation created by the Petroleum Corporation Act (assented 7 November 1973) to buy and sell natural gas and petroleum; partially privatized in 1990 and dissolved in September 1994, its functions absorbed by the Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources.

name: Human Rights Commission
description: Established by the Human Rights Code of British Columbia Act of 1973; replaced by the BC Council of Human Rights in 1984.

name: British Columbia Assessment Authority
description: Independent Crown corporation that values all real property in the province, created by the Assessment Authority Act (Royal Assent 2 July 1974).

name: Emergency Health Services Commission
description: Commission created by legislation in 1974 to provide a provincial ambulance service (BC Ambulance Service) and medical disaster planning; became BC Emergency Health Services, a PHSA division, in 2013.

name: Legal Services Commission
description: Commission established August 1975, replacing the Legal Services Division; amalgamated with the Legal Aid Society of B.C. on 1 October 1979 to form the Legal Services Society.

name: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd.
description: Crown corporation created in 1975 to restore Victoria-Seattle passenger and car service with the Princess Marguerite, bought from Canadian Pacific; dissolved in 1992.

name: British Columbia Buildings Corporation
description: Crown corporation that served as the government's landlord (over 3,400 buildings by 1994), established 30 June 1976 and dissolved in 2006 under the Public Agency Accommodation Act.

name: British Columbia Systems Corporation
description: Crown corporation created under the System Act on 1 September 1977 to provide data-processing and telecommunications services to ministries; broken up in 1996.

name: British Columbia Resources Investment Corporation
description: Holding company for Crown-owned mills and mines bought in 1972-75, known for the free 'Brick' shares of 1979; renamed Westar Group Ltd. and made a publicly traded company, no longer a Crown corporation, by a 1988 amendment.

name: British Columbia Heritage Trust
description: Crown corporation established under the Heritage Conservation Act of 1977 to fund heritage conservation; its operations were terminated on 31 March 2003 after the Core Services Review.

name: Provincial Capital Commission
description: Crown agency (successor to the Capital Improvement District Commission) that stewarded capital-region heritage properties such as the Crystal Garden and St. Ann's Academy; its elimination was announced in November 2013 and it was dissolved in 2014.

name: BC Games Society
description: Crown corporation created in 1977 to run the BC Summer and Winter Games and manage Team BC at the Canada Games.

name: Open Learning Institute
description: Distance-education institute created in 1978 under the BC Colleges and Provincial Institutes Act; combined with the Knowledge Network into the Open Learning Agency in 1988.

name: Science Council of British Columbia
description: Crown agency created in 1978 under the Science Council Act to promote science and technology; its Act was retitled the Innovation and Science Council Act in 2003 and it became the BC Innovation Council in 2004.

name: British Columbia Film Commission
description: Provincial film-promotion office founded in 1978 under Tourism Minister Grace McCarthy; merged with BC Film + Media in April 2013 to form Creative BC.

name: Expo 86 Corporation
description: Provincial nonprofit agency, set up under the Transpo 86 Corporation Act of 1980, that planned and ran the Expo 86 world's fair (2 May-13 October 1986), headed by Jim Pattison.

name: Urban Transit Authority
description: Crown corporation created in 1979 to coordinate planning, marketing and funding of municipal transit; took over Victoria and Vancouver transit from BC Hydro in 1980 and was renamed BC Transit in 1982.

name: Metro Transit Operating Company
description: Crown corporation established by the Metro Transit Operating Company Act to operate Vancouver-area transit; merged with the Urban Transit Authority into BC Transit.

name: Legal Services Society
description: Statutory legal-aid provider formed on 1 October 1979 by amalgamating the Legal Services Commission and the Legal Aid Society of B.C.; it now operates as Legal Aid BC.

name: British Columbia Place Ltd.
description: Crown corporation established May 1980 (developer of BC Place); renamed British Columbia Enterprise Corporation in March 1987.

name: BC Transit
description: Provincial transit Crown corporation, renamed from the Urban Transit Authority in 1982; it handed Metro Vancouver transit to TransLink in 1999 and now coordinates transit elsewhere in the province.

name: British Columbia Utilities Commission
description: Independent regulator of energy utilities, pipelines and ICBC basic insurance rates, established by the Utilities Commission Act in 1980.

name: W.L.C. Developments Ltd.
description: Crown-owned company established January 1983 to develop and sell Crown land in Whistler; its mandate was broadened in 1997 and it was renamed in 1998.

name: B.C. Pavilion Corporation
description: Crown corporation incorporated in 1984 under the Company Act that took over BC Enterprise Corporation's remaining assets in 1989 and operates BC Place and the Vancouver Convention Centre.

name: British Columbia Lottery Corporation
description: Crown corporation incorporated 25 October 1984 that began selling lottery tickets in 1985 after B.C. left the Western Canada Lottery Foundation; it now also runs casino and online gambling.

name: BC Council of Human Rights
description: Body that replaced the Human Rights Commission in 1984; replaced in 1997 by a new Human Rights Commission, Advisory Council and Tribunal.

name: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation
description: Crown corporation formed in March 1987 by renaming BC Place Ltd. and merging in the BC Development Corporation; it ceased operations on 30 September 1989, transferring its assets to the Province and B.C. Pavilion Corporation.

name: Open Learning Agency
description: Crown agency established by legislation early in 1988, combining the Knowledge Network with the Open Learning Institute; its university function moved to Thompson Rivers University in 2005 and it was continued as the Knowledge Network Corporation in 2007.

name: Financial Institutions Commission
description: Regulator of credit unions, insurance and trust companies, pension plans and mortgage brokers from 1989 until it was replaced by the BC Financial Services Authority in 2019.

name: First Peoples' Cultural Council
description: First Nations-governed Crown corporation established in 1990 under the First Peoples' Heritage, Language and Culture Act to support Indigenous language, arts and culture.

name: British Columbia Treaty Commission
description: Independent body co-established in 1992 by Canada, British Columbia and the First Nations Summit to facilitate treaty negotiations, later given provincial and federal statutory footing.

name: BC Transportation Financing Authority
description: Crown corporation established in 1993 under the Build BC Act (the Transportation Act replaced it as its basis on 31 December 2004) to plan, acquire, build and hold transportation infrastructure. It owns BC Railway Company (from 1 April 2010) and Transportation Investment Corporation (from 1 April 2018).

name: Columbia Power Corporation
description: Crown corporation created in 1994 to buy hydroelectric rights from Cominco, later developing Columbia Basin power projects with the Columbia Basin Trust.

name: Forest Renewal BC
description: Crown corporation created under the Forest Renewal Act of 1994 to reinvest stumpage revenue in forests and forest communities; the Act was repealed effective 27 June 2002 and a forest investment account replaced it.

name: Forest Practices Board
description: Independent watchdog for forest and range practices, established under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act of 1994 (code proclaimed 15 June 1995).

name: Columbia Basin Trust
description: Regional trust created by the Columbia Basin Trust Act in 1995 to benefit the region most affected by the Columbia River Treaty.

name: British Columbia Securities Commission
description: Self-funded Crown corporation created on 1 April 1995 to administer the Securities Act and regulate capital markets.

name: British Columbia Arts Council
description: Statutory agency created by the BC Arts Council Act of 1995 to fund the arts.

name: Tourism British Columbia
description: Crown corporation established in 1997 to market the province to tourists; merged into the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and the Arts on 1 April 2010.

name: BC Human Rights Commission
description: Commission created by the Human Rights Amendment Act of 1995 to investigate complaints alongside the new Tribunal; abolished by the Campbell government in 2003.

name: BC Human Rights Tribunal
description: Adjudicative body under the Human Rights Code, created by the Human Rights Amendment Act of 1995 and hearing cases since 1997; took over complaint screening when the Commission was abolished in 2003.

name: Industry Training and Apprenticeship Commission
description: Arm's-length commission of business, labour, education and government, announced 23 June 1997 to govern industry training and apprenticeship; dissolved in 2003.

name: British Columbia Assets and Land Corporation
description: Renamed from W.L.C. Developments in 1998 to sell surplus Crown land and administer Crown land tenures; renamed Land and Water British Columbia Inc. in 2002.

name: Greater Vancouver Transportation Authority
description: Statutory regional transportation authority created in 1998 and fully in operation in April 1999, replacing BC Transit in Greater Vancouver.

name: BC Oil and Gas Commission
description: Crown regulator of oil and gas activities and pipelines, established in October 1998 under the Oil and Gas Commission Act.

name: British Columbia Investment Management Corporation
description: Investment manager for public-sector pension plans, created by the Public Sector Pension Plans Act of 1999 to take over assets managed by the Ministry of Finance.

name: British Columbia Pension Corporation
description: Pension administration agent for the College, Municipal, Public Service, Teachers' and WorkSafeBC plans, created in 2000 under the Public Sector Pension Plans Act.

name: Merit Commissioner
description: Office created in 2001 (an independent officer of the Legislature from 2005) to audit merit-based public-service hiring; dissolved by the Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2026, with the role transferred to the head of the BC Public Service Agency.

name: Fraser Health Authority
description: One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates three regional boards into it: the Fraser Valley, Simon Fraser and South Fraser health regions.

name: Interior Health Authority
description: One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates seventeen bodies into it: the Thompson, North Okanagan and Okanagan Similkameen health regions and fourteen councils and transitional authorities of the Kootenays and Cariboo. The East Kootenay, Kootenay Boundary and most of the Cariboo community health services societies’ services passed to it at the same time.

name: Northern Health Authority
description: One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates thirteen bodies into it: the Northern Interior Regional Health Board and twelve northwest, northeast and Quesnel councils. The North West and Peace Liard societies’ services, and the Cariboo society’s in Quesnel, passed to it at the same time.

name: Vancouver Coastal Health Authority
description: One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates five bodies into it: the Vancouver/Richmond Health Board, the North Shore Health Region and the Powell River, Sea to Sky and Sunshine Coast councils; the Coast Garibaldi society’s services passed to it. The Bella Coola and Central Coast areas joined it from Interior and Vancouver Island on 18 March 2002.

name: Vancouver Island Health Authority
description: One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates six bodies into it: the Capital and Central Vancouver Island health regions and four councils and transitional authorities of the north island and Central Coast; the Upper Island/Central Coast society’s services passed to it. The Central Coast area moved to Vancouver Coastal on 18 March 2002.

name: Provincial Health Services Authority
description: Province-wide health authority, incorporated under the Society Act on 12 December 2001 to coordinate specialized provincial services: the BC Cancer Agency, BC Centre for Disease Control, BC Provincial Renal Agency, BC Transplant Society, Children’s and Women’s Health Centre, Riverview Hospital, Forensic Psychiatric Services and others. It is not a successor of the regional boards; its agencies each have their own history, and their branch societies were amalgamated with it into one society on 1 April 2018. Its mandate was refocused after a 2025 review.

name: Partnerships British Columbia
description: Crown corporation created in 2002 to plan and procure public-private partnership infrastructure projects; began operating as Infrastructure BC in January 2021.

name: Land and Water British Columbia Inc.
description: BCAL renamed in 2002 with an expanded mandate over water licensing and allocation as well as Crown land; eliminated in the 2005 government reorganization.

name: British Columbia Transmission Corporation
description: Crown corporation formed under the Transmission Corporation Act of 2003 to operate BC Hydro's transmission system independently; re-merged into BC Hydro in 2010 under the Clean Energy Act.

name: Royal British Columbia Museum
description: Provincial museum founded in 1886, styled 'Royal' from 1987, which merged with the BC Provincial Archives in 2003 and is listed as a provincial Crown corporation.

name: Industry Training Authority
description: Agency established in 2004 to replace ITAC after mandatory trades certification was abolished in 2003; renamed SkilledTradesBC in December 2022.

name: BC Innovation Council
description: Crown agency formed in 2004 by merging the Advanced Science Institute BC (as Wikipedia styles it) and the Innovation and Science Council of British Columbia; renamed Innovate BC in 2018.

name: BC Safety Authority
description: Independent technical-safety regulator since 2004; adopted the operating name Technical Safety BC on 20 September 2017.

name: Northern Development Initiative Trust
description: Regional economic-development trust for central and northern B.C., created by the Northern Development Initiative Trust Act (Bill 59, introduced 6 October 2004) with proceeds from the BC Rail deal.

name: Community Living British Columbia
description: Crown agency under the Community Living Authority Act, incorporated 1 July 2005, providing supports for adults with developmental disabilities.

name: Island Coastal Economic Trust
description: One of three provincially funded regional economic trusts, created in 2006 for Vancouver Island and the coast.

name: Knowledge Network Corporation
description: The Open Learning Agency continued under the Knowledge Network Corporation Act (assented 31 May 2007) as the Crown owner of the public educational broadcaster, on air since 12 January 1981.

name: South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority
description: TransLink's official name after legislation approved 29 November 2007 changed the authority's governance and name; it runs Metro Vancouver's regional transit, major roads and bridges.

name: Pacific Carbon Trust
description: Crown carbon-offset agency established in 2008; its elimination was announced on 19 November 2013 and its offset program was moved into the Environment Ministry.

name: Transportation Investment Corporation
description: Crown corporation established in 2008 under the Transportation Investment Act to deliver the Port Mann/Highway 1 project, later other major transportation projects.

name: Destination BC Corp.
description: Crown corporation created under the Business Corporations Act on 2 November 2012 (operating from 1 April 2013) to market B.C. tourism, reversing the 2010 absorption of Tourism BC into government.

name: Creative BC
description: Agency formed in April 2013 by merging the BC Film Commission and BC Film + Media to develop the province's creative industries.

name: BC Emergency Health Services
description: The Emergency and Health Services Commission renamed and made a division of PHSA in 2013; it runs BC Ambulance Service.

name: Technical Safety BC
description: Operating name adopted by the BC Safety Authority on 20 September 2017.

name: Innovate BC
description: Crown agency funding technology start-up and commercialization programs, renamed from the BC Innovation Council in 2018.

name: BC Financial Services Authority
description: Crown agency that replaced FICOM in November 2019 and on 1 August 2021 absorbed the Real Estate Council of BC and the Superintendent of Real Estate's office.

name: Infrastructure BC
description: Operating name, adopted in January 2021, of the Crown corporation formerly Partnerships BC, with an expanded project-procurement mandate.

name: InBC Investment Corp.
description: Crown corporation set up in 2021 as the Province's $500-million strategic investment fund; its board was appointed on 6 May 2021.

name: SkilledTradesBC
description: The Industry Training Authority renamed in December 2022 as the government reintroduced mandatory skilled-trades certification.

name: British Columbia Energy Regulator
description: The Oil and Gas Commission renamed under the Energy Statutes Amendment Act, 2022 (name change announced February 2023), with a mandate expanded to hydrogen, methanol and ammonia.

name: BC Shared Health Services
description: Stand-alone shared-services society, announced in December 2025 after the health-authority review and incorporated on 1 April 2026, to provide corporate and administrative services to the health authorities. It is a member of the Health Employers Association of BC, not a part of it, and its functions move to it in waves after incorporation.

name: British Columbia Farm Industry Review Board
description: Supervises B.C.'s agricultural marketing boards and commissions and hears appeals and complaints on marketing decisions, farm practices and animal seizures.

name: Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch
description: Regulates and licenses the provincial liquor and cannabis sectors under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act and the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act.
note: Responsibility moved to Agriculture and Food in July 2025; per the PSSG 2026/27 service plan, oversight is shared with PSSG, where compliance and enforcement functions remain.

name: Animal Health Centre
description: The Province's animal health diagnostic laboratory, providing pathology, bacteriology, virology, toxicology and other testing for animals in B.C.

name: AgriService BC
description: Point of contact for information on provincial programs, resources and services for agriculture, aquaculture, fisheries, seafood and food-processing businesses.

name: Agriculture Insurance and Income Protection programs
description: Business risk management programs for farmers, including Production Insurance, AgriStability, AgriInvest and agriculture wildlife damage compensation.
note: Production Insurance is funded through the Production Insurance Account special account (2026/27 Estimates).

name: Buy BC
description: Provincial food-marketing program that helps British Columbians identify and choose food and beverages grown, raised or made in B.C.

name: Feed BC
description: Works with government and industry partners to bring more B.C. food into B.C. government facilities such as hospitals and post-secondary institutions.

name: BC Prosecution Service
description: Conducts criminal prosecutions and appeals on behalf of the Crown under the Crown Counsel Act, acting independently of police and government.

name: Court Services Branch
description: Provides court registries, court administration, juror support, transcript services and sheriff services to the Court of Appeal, Supreme Court and Provincial Court.

name: BC Sheriff Services
description: Provides court security, prisoner escort, document service and warrant services under the Sheriff Act.
note: Part of Court Services Branch per the AG org chart; duties from the Court Services sub-vote in the 2026/27 Estimates.

name: Legal Services Branch
description: Government's in-house law office, giving legal advice, conducting civil litigation for the Province and drafting legislation through the Office of Legislative Counsel.

name: Family Justice Services Division
description: Promotes the timely and just resolution of family disputes through information, dispute resolution and parenting programs, and runs the Justice Access Centres.

name: Public Guardian and Trustee of British Columbia
description: Helps people who need assistance with decision-making or are under 19 and administers deceased estates.
note: Listed among AG agencies on the AG org chart; funded partly through the Public Guardian and Trustee Operating Account (2026/27 Estimates).

name: Independent Investigations Office of BC
description: Civilian-led office that investigates incidents where the actions or inactions of police may have caused serious injury or death.
note: Has its own vote (Vote 17) under the Ministry of Attorney General.

name: Civil Resolution Tribunal
description: Canada's first online tribunal, resolving strata, small claims, minor vehicle injury, intimate image and other disputes without the need to go to court.

name: Indigenous Justice Secretariat
description: Joint commitment with the BC First Nations Justice Council to reduce the overrepresentation of Indigenous people in the justice system and rebuild Indigenous justice systems.

name: Multiculturalism and Anti-Racism Branch
description: Delivers multiculturalism and anti-racism programs, including support for the Resilience BC Anti-Racism Network.

name: Intimate Images Protection Service
description: Supports people whose intimate images have been shared, or threatened to be shared, without consent.
note: Public-facing brand: Take Back Your Images. Parent inferred from its link on the AG ministry page.

name: Provincial Centralized Screening
description: Around-the-clock line (1-800-663-9122) for reporting suspected abuse or neglect of a child or youth to a child welfare worker.

name: Child and Youth Mental Health Services
description: Community clinics and specialized services that assess and treat children and youth with mental health issues.

name: Maples Adolescent Treatment Centre
description: Adolescent mental health facility operated by the ministry, including services under the Mental Health Act.
note: Facility; named in the Child and Youth Mental Health Services sub-vote of the 2026/27 Estimates.

name: Youth Justice Services
description: Community and custody programs for youth in conflict with the law, including youth custody centres and youth forensic psychiatric services.

name: Children and Youth with Support Needs
description: Early intervention, therapy, respite and family support for children and youth with support needs.

name: Adoption Services
description: Recruits adoptive families, plans permanency for children in care and provides post-adoption assistance under the Adoption Act.

name: Foster caregiving and kinship care
description: Recruits and supports foster and extended-family caregivers who give homes to children and youth unable to live with their own families.

name: Early Childhood Development
description: Funds early childhood development programs aimed at infants, young children and their families.

name: Service BC
description: Government's front door for in-person, phone and online services, from driver's licences and health cards to business registration.

name: Connected Services BC
description: Leads strategy, policy and standards for government telecommunications, information technology, IT security and the IM/IT investment portfolio.
note: Described in the 2026/27 service plan as a new organization within the ministry. The Office of the Chief Information Officer is not named in current sources; its former functions appear to sit here.

name: BC Registries and Online Services
description: Administers registrations of businesses, societies, cooperatives, personal property and manufactured homes.

name: BC OnLine
description: Fee-based online service giving professional users access to provincial registry and other government data.

name: BC Services Card
description: Provincial identification card used to access health coverage and other government services, in person and online.

name: BC Stats
description: The provincial government's statistical office, providing statistics, economic research and analysis under the Statistics Act.
note: BC Stats' own page does not name its ministry; parent is inferred from the 2026/27 Citizens' Services service plan, which assigns statistical and economic research to the ministry.

name: Connectivity in B.C.
description: Funds and coordinates expansion of high-speed internet and highway cellular coverage in rural, remote and Indigenous communities.

name: BC Bid
description: The Province's online marketplace for public-sector procurement opportunities.

name: Asset Investment Recovery
description: Disposes of surplus government assets, including through the BC Auction website.
note: BC Auction is its public sales site (linked from the ministry page).

name: King's Printer
description: Full cost-recovery publishing service for government, including official print and publication services.

name: Product Distribution Centre
description: Full cost-recovery warehousing and product distribution service for ministries and the broader public sector.

name: ChildCareBC
description: Provincial child care program lowering fees for families, opening new licensed spaces and training early learning professionals.

name: Early Childhood Educator Registry
description: Certifies early childhood educators under the Community Care and Assisted Living Act.

name: Commissioner for Teacher Regulation
description: Statutory decision-maker who handles complaints and discipline of certified teachers in B.C.

name: BC Teachers' Council
description: Sets standards for B.C. educators and teacher education programs under the Teachers Act.

name: StrongStart BC
description: Free drop-in early learning programs for children up to age five and their parents or caregivers, usually in schools.

name: Child Care Resource and Referral Centres
description: Community centres that help families find and access quality child care.

name: Feeding Futures
description: Funding for school food programs in B.C. public schools.

name: erase (expect respect & a safe education)
description: Helps students, adults and school staff build safe, caring and inclusive school communities.

name: British Columbia Training and Education Savings Program
description: Provincial education savings program run through a special account under the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act.

name: Emergency Support Services
description: Provides evacuees with basic supports such as accommodation, food and clothing, backed by the BC Evacuee Helpline.

name: Disaster Financial Assistance
description: Financial help for homeowners, renters, businesses and local governments recovering from uninsurable disaster losses under the Emergency and Disaster Management Act.

name: PreparedBC
description: British Columbia's one-stop shop for disaster readiness information.

name: EmergencyInfoBC
description: Official source of current information during emergencies in B.C.

name: ClimateReadyBC
description: Online platform to help the public and communities understand disaster and climate risks and find funding to build resilience.

name: Disaster Resilience Division
description: Leads provincial disaster and climate risk assessment and risk-reduction work, including the Disaster and Climate Risk and Resilience Assessment.

name: Climate Action Secretariat
description: Leads the Province's climate policy, greenhouse gas reporting and climate accountability work.
note: Moved to this ministry per the 2025/26 service plan; the 2026/27 Estimates carry the work under the Climate Action sub-vote. The 2026/27 service plan does not name it.

name: CleanBC
description: The Province's climate plan and program brand for cutting emissions, building a cleaner economy and preparing communities.

name: B.C. Output-Based Pricing System
description: Carbon-pricing system for large industrial emitters that gives a price incentive to cut emissions while addressing carbon leakage.

name: CleanBC Industry Fund
description: Funds industrial projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
note: The fetched page is titled 'Clean Industry Fund'.

name: B.C. Low Carbon Fuel Standard
description: Requirements under the Low Carbon Fuels Act that reduce the carbon intensity of transportation fuels, with a credit market for compliance.

name: Innovative Clean Energy Fund
description: Special account funding clean energy technology projects.

name: First Nations Clean Energy Business Fund
description: Special account under the Clean Energy Act that supports First Nations' participation in the clean energy sector.

name: Climate Solutions Council
description: Advisory council that advises government on climate action and clean growth.

name: BC Parks
description: Manages B.C.'s provincial parks and protected areas.

name: Conservation Officer Service
description: Public safety provider focused on natural resource law enforcement and on preventing and responding to human-wildlife conflicts.

name: Environmental Assessment Office
description: Runs the neutral assessment process under the Environmental Assessment Act for major projects and enforces certified projects' conditions.
note: Has its own vote (Vote 25) under Environment and Parks.

name: Recreation Sites and Trails BC
description: Develops, maintains and manages a province-wide network of recreation sites and trails.

name: Report All Poachers and Polluters
description: Toll-free tip line and web service for reporting known or suspected violations of fisheries, wildlife or environmental protection laws.

name: Park Enhancement Fund
description: Special account that funds improvements in B.C. parks.

name: Sustainable Environment Fund
description: Statutory fund under the Sustainable Environment Fund Act that supports environmental protection.

name: Treasury Board Staff
description: Advises Treasury Board and builds the provincial budget, three-year fiscal plan, Estimates and quarterly reports.

name: Office of the Comptroller General
description: Maintains the government's financial control framework, administers the central accounts and prepares the Public Accounts.

name: Provincial Treasury
description: Handles the Province's borrowing, debt management, banking and cash management.

name: Revenue Division
description: Administers and enforces provincial tax and revenue statutes and related benefit, loan and collection programs.

name: Gender Equity Office
description: Leads government-wide gender equity work, including pay transparency and Gender-Based Analysis Plus.

name: Public Sector Employers' Council Secretariat
description: Coordinates labour relations, compensation planning and HR management across the broader provincial public sector.

name: Crown Agencies Secretariat
description: Central agency in the Ministry of Finance that provides governance support and oversight for public sector organizations.

name: Crown Agencies and Board Resourcing Office
description: Recruits and recommends candidates for appointment to Crown corporations, agencies, boards and commissions.

name: Internal Audit & Advisory Services
description: Carries out internal audits of ministries, Crown corporations and the broader public sector.
note: Part of the Office of the Comptroller General.

name: Government Chief Risk Office
description: Central risk-management agency for ministries and the broader public sector.
note: Located within Provincial Treasury; the Government Security Office is also located there.

name: Anti-Money Laundering Secretariat
description: Coordinates the Province's anti-money-laundering work.
note: Administered within the Revenue Division sub-vote in the 2026/27 Estimates.

name: BC Wildfire Service
description: Manages wildfire prevention and response across B.C. through six regional fire centres.

name: BC Timber Sales
description: Manages 20 per cent of B.C.'s public timber harvest and sells Crown timber at auction.

name: Office of the Chief Forester
description: Leads timber supply review and allowable annual cut decisions, forest inventory, forest genetics, silviculture and forest health programs.

name: Archaeology Branch
description: Protects archaeological sites under the Heritage Conservation Act and issues archaeology permits.

name: Tree Improvement Branch
description: Protects, manages and conserves B.C.'s forest genetic resources, including tree seed.

name: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
description: Office of B.C.'s senior public health official, who monitors population health and gives independent advice under the Public Health Act.

name: Medical Services Plan
description: The provincial health insurance plan, covering most physician, diagnostic and laboratory services for residents.

name: BC PharmaCare
description: Publicly funded program that helps B.C. residents pay for some prescription drugs, medical supplies and pharmacy services.

name: HealthLink BC
description: 24/7 provincial health information and advice service, including 8-1-1.
note: Linked from the Ministry of Health page; operating arrangements not confirmed in the sources read.

name: Health Connect Registry
description: Provincial waitlist that connects people to a family doctor or nurse practitioner.

name: Office of the Seniors Advocate
description: Monitors and reports on services for seniors, including health care, housing, transportation and income supports.
note: Funded within the Ministry of Health's Health Programs sub-vote (2026/27 Estimates).

name: Office of Indigenous Health
description: Ministry of Health office for Indigenous health.

name: Patient Care Quality Review Boards
description: Six independent boards under the Patient Care Quality Review Board Act that review care complaints.

name: HelpStartsHere
description: Searchable directory of mental health and substance use services in B.C.

name: Residential Tenancy Branch
description: Provides information and dispute resolution for landlords and tenants under the Residential Tenancy and Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Acts.

name: Short-Term Rental Branch
description: Administers provincial short-term rental rules and the short-term rental registry, including a compliance and enforcement unit.

name: Building and Safety Standards
description: Oversees the BC Building, Plumbing and Fire Codes, the Building Act and technical safety standards.
note: Branch name as given in the ministry page link; the Estimates place this work in the Building, Governance and Innovation sub-vote.

name: Public Libraries Branch
description: Supports and funds B.C.'s public library system.

name: University Endowment Lands
description: The ministry provides local services and oversees land use in the University Endowment Lands.

name: Housing Targets program
description: Sets and monitors housing supply targets for selected municipalities under the Housing Supply Act.

name: Declaration Act Secretariat
description: Central agency that guides government to align provincial laws with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
note: Has its own vote (Vote 36) under the ministry.

name: First Citizens Fund
description: Special account supporting Indigenous cultural, educational and economic initiatives.

name: Government to Government and Community Relations Division
description: Negotiates and implements treaties, incremental treaty agreements, reconciliation and revenue-sharing agreements with First Nations.

name: Policy, Intergovernmental Relations and Legislation Division
description: Leads reconciliation policy and cost-sharing negotiations with the federal government for treaties and other agreements.

name: Programs and Partnerships Division
description: Supports Indigenous organizations, culture and language initiatives and cross-government work on the UN Declaration.

name: Minister's Advisory Council on Indigenous Women
description: Advises the Province on improving the quality of life of Indigenous women.

name: Real Property Division
description: Manages the Province's office and special-purpose real estate portfolio, including leasing and workplace services.
note: Transferred from the Ministry of Citizens' Services in December 2025.

name: Community Capital Development
description: Plans, procures and manages capital projects for schools, child care, hospitals and post-secondary facilities.

name: Policy and Partnerships
description: Develops policy, programs and legislation for provincial vertical capital infrastructure projects.

name: Trade and Invest British Columbia
description: International trade and investment service, including the Province's network of international trade offices.

name: Small Business Roundtable
description: Advisory roundtable on small business issues operated by the ministry.

name: EaseBiz BC
description: Ease-of-doing-business initiative that engages the business community to find and remove barriers.

name: BizPaL
description: Online service listing the permits and licences a business needs.

name: Employment Standards Branch
description: Administers the Employment Standards Act and Regulation, which set minimum wages and working conditions.

name: Workers' Advisers Office
description: Free advice and assistance for workers and dependants in disputes with WorkSafeBC decisions.

name: Employers' Advisers Office
description: Free advice, representation and education for employers on workers' compensation and occupational health and safety.

name: Employment Standards Tribunal
description: Hears appeals of determinations issued by the Director of Employment Standards.
note: Administrative support is funded through the Attorney General's tribunals sub-vote (2026/27 Estimates).

name: Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal
description: Independent tribunal that hears appeals of WorkSafeBC decisions.

name: British Columbia Geological Survey
description: Provides geoscience data, surveys and mineral and coal resource information for B.C.

name: Mineral Development Office
description: Vancouver base of the BC Geological Survey that links it with the exploration and mining companies headquartered there.

name: Critical Minerals Office
description: Supports the advancement of B.C. critical minerals projects.

name: Mineral Titles Online
description: Online registry for acquiring and managing mineral, placer and coal titles.

name: Mines Health, Safety and Enforcement
description: Oversees health, safety and reclamation at all mineral, coal and aggregate mines through inspections, investigations and enforcement.
note: Publishes the Chief Inspector of Mines' annual reports (Mining Health and Safety page).

name: StudentAid BC
description: Provides student loans, grants and other financial help for post-secondary learners.

name: BC Provincial Nominee Program
description: Economic immigration program that nominates workers and entrepreneurs for permanent residence in B.C.

name: Private Training Institutions Branch
description: Regulates private training institutions certified under the Private Training Act and administers the Student Tuition Protection Fund.
note: Estimates name the function 'Private Training Institutions'; branch name confirmed only in web-search snippets.

name: Office for International Credential Recognition
description: Oversees how professional regulators assess the credentials of internationally trained professionals seeking work in B.C.

name: BC Newcomers Services Program
description: Immigrant settlement and integration services for newcomers to B.C.

name: EducationPlannerBC
description: Online service for planning, searching and applying to public post-secondary institutions in B.C.

name: Safe Campuses BC
description: Initiative to make post-secondary campuses safe for everyone.

name: Education Quality Assurance
description: Designation that public and private post-secondary institutions need to enrol international students with study permits.

name: BC Coroners Service
description: Investigates unnatural, sudden and unexpected deaths, holds inquests and death review panels and makes prevention recommendations.

name: BC Corrections
description: Manages remanded and sentenced adult offenders in custody and in the community.

name: Civil Forfeiture Office
description: Uses civil court proceedings to take the proceeds and instruments of unlawful activity.
note: Part of the Community Safety and Victim Services division per the PSSG org chart.

name: Community Safety and Victim Services
description: Supports victims of crime, including financial assistance and counselling, and funds community crime prevention.

name: VictimLinkBC
description: Province-wide, around-the-clock information and referral line for victims of crime.

name: Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch
description: Regulates gambling in B.C., including lotteries and horse racing, and runs the responsible and problem gambling programs.

name: Office of the Fire Commissioner
description: Administers the Fire Safety Act through fire inspections, investigations, prevention and support for local fire services.

name: Policing and Security Branch
description: Superintends policing and law enforcement in B.C., manages contract policing and regulates the security industry.

name: RoadSafetyBC
description: Leads traffic safety, sets driver licensing policy, monitors unfit drivers and reviews driving prohibitions.
note: Headed by the Superintendent of Motor Vehicles.

name: Security Programs
description: Licenses the security industry, including security workers, armoured vehicles and body armour.
note: Part of Policing and Security per the PSSG org chart.

name: Criminal Records Review Program
description: Provides criminal record checks for people who work with children or vulnerable adults.

name: Compliance and Enforcement Collaborative
description: Cross-government compliance and enforcement body housed in the ministry's Corporate Strategic Initiatives division.
note: Estimates call it the Compliance and Enforcement Secretariat; the central-agencies page calls it the Compliance and Enforcement Collaborative.

name: WorkBC
description: Provincial employment services that help people find and keep jobs, plus online career and labour market resources.
note: SDPR delivers the employment services; PSEFS also uses WorkBC.ca for labour market information.

name: Employment and Assistance Appeal Tribunal
description: Single-level, community-based tribunal hearing appeals of the ministry's reconsideration decisions on income and disability assistance.

name: Accessibility Directorate
description: Supports the implementation of the Accessible British Columbia Act and coordinates government's accessibility plan.

name: Provincial Accessibility Committee
description: Advisory committee supporting implementation of the Accessible British Columbia Act.

name: Income and Disability Assistance
description: Income assistance, disability assistance, hardship assistance and supplements under the Employment and Assistance Acts.

name: My Self Serve
description: Online portal for people applying for or receiving income and disability assistance.

name: BC Bus Pass Program
description: Reduced-cost annual TransLink or BC Transit bus pass for eligible low-income seniors and people on disability assistance.

name: Single Parent Employment Initiative
description: Training and employment supports for single parents receiving assistance.

name: Community Gaming Grants
description: Distributes gaming revenue to community non-profits in arts and culture, sport, public safety, environment, parent advisory councils and human and social services.

name: Office of the BC Athletic Commissioner
description: Oversees professional boxing, kickboxing and MMA and all amateur combat sports events in B.C.

name: Heritage Branch
description: Supports the conservation of heritage values on the land base through policy, programs, provincial heritage sites and partnerships.
note: Part of TACS since April 2022.

name: Mountain Resorts Branch
description: Administers all-season resort development on Crown land in B.C.

name: Let's Go BC
description: Program for hosting major sporting events in B.C. and building lasting legacies from them.

name: BC Arts and Culture Endowment
description: Special account holding the BC150 Cultural Fund and Arts Legacy Fund.

name: Physical Fitness and Amateur Sports Fund
description: Special account supporting sport and physical activity in B.C.

name: DriveBC
description: Real-time information on B.C. road conditions, closures, highway webcams and delays.

name: Inland Ferries
description: B.C.'s free inland ferry system, operated and maintained by the ministry.

name: Commercial Vehicle Safety and Enforcement
description: Enforces commercial vehicle safety through inspection stations and runs commercial transport permitting.

name: Passenger Transportation Branch
description: Licenses and enforces rules for commercial passenger vehicles under the Passenger Transportation Act.

name: Office of the B.C. Container Trucking Commissioner
description: Enforces the Container Trucking Act, issues container trucking licences and sets rates.
note: The TRAN 2026/27 service plan describes the ministry as its principal liaison into government.

name: B.C. River Forecast Centre
description: Monitors and models streamflow, snow and flood conditions across British Columbia.

name: B.C. Drought Information Portal
description: Single source for provincial drought levels, watershed conditions and drought history.

name: Water licensing and rights
description: Authorizes the use of Crown-owned surface water and groundwater under the Water Sustainability Act.

name: Caribou Recovery Program
description: Provincial program to transform caribou management and recover caribou populations.

name: Together for Wildlife
description: Provincial strategy to help wildlife and their habitats thrive.

name: Permit Connect B.C.
description: Coordinates permitting for the Province's priority projects, including housing.

name: FrontCounter BC
description: Single window for natural resource clients seeking information and authorizations.
note: Parent inferred from the Estimates, which put natural-resource permitting and authorizations in the WLRS Permitting Transformation sub-vote; the page itself does not name a ministry.

name: Planning in Partnership
description: Public engagement site for land and water use planning in B.C.

name: Civil Resolution Tribunal
description: Canada's first online tribunal, resolving strata, small claims up to $5,000, vehicle accident, intimate image, and society and cooperative disputes.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Created under the Civil Resolution Tribunal Act; launched July 13, 2016 (CRT about page).

name: British Columbia Review Board
description: Tribunal constituted under the Criminal Code that makes and reviews dispositions for accused persons found unfit to stand trial or not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: Building Code Appeal Board
description: Resolves disputes under the Building Act about whether a matter conforms to a provincial building regulation such as the BC Building and Plumbing Codes.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. A member of the Building and Safety Standards Branch serves as board secretary (board page).

name: Community Care and Assisted Living Appeal Board
description: Hears appeals of licensing, registration and certification decisions about community care facilities, assisted living residences and early childhood educators under the Community Care and Assisted Living Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: Employment Standards Tribunal
description: Hears appeals of determinations issued by the Director of Employment Standards under the Employment Standards Act and the Temporary Foreign Worker Protection Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Established November 1, 1995 (EST about page). The Ministry of Labour 2026/27 service plan also calls it one of 'the Ministry's three tribunals' (legislative responsibility), so ministry-of-labour-2017 is an alternative parent.

name: Energy Resource Appeal Tribunal
description: Hears appeals of certain orders, penalties and permitting decisions of the BC Energy Regulator under the Oil and Gas Activities Act as amended in 2023.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Former name Oil and Gas Appeal Tribunal: the old ogat.gov.bc.ca domain linked from the tribunal-sector page redirects to bcerat.ca, and ERAT decisions carry OGAT file numbers.

name: Environmental Appeal Board
description: Decides appeals of certain government decisions under nine provincial statutes on environmental issues such as water licences, contaminated sites, pesticides and hunting licences.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. EAB site: 'established under the Environment Management Act (1981)'; now operates under the Environmental Management Act.

name: Financial Services Tribunal
description: Hears appeals of enforcement decisions by the Insurance Council of BC, the Superintendents of Real Estate, Pensions and Financial Institutions, and the Registrar of Mortgage Brokers.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Established in 2004 under s. 242.1 of the Financial Institutions Act (FST about page).

name: Forest Appeals Commission
description: Decides appeals of certain decisions under five provincial statutes on forests and environmental issues, now operating under the Forest and Range Practices Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: Health Professions Review Board
description: Reviews certain registration and complaint decisions of the health profession regulatory colleges, now under the Health Professions and Occupations Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. HPRB site now says it is established under the Health Professions and Occupations Act (in force April 1, 2026).

name: Hospital Appeal Board
description: Hears medical practitioners' appeals of hospital board of management decisions affecting hospital privileges under the Hospital Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. 'Originally established as the Medical Appeal Board in 1973' (HAB about page).

name: Mental Health Review Board
description: Conducts review panel hearings on whether people certified or detained involuntarily in provincial mental health facilities should remain so under the Mental Health Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. 'Established in April 2005' (MHRB home page).

name: Passenger Transportation Board
description: Independent tribunal that licenses and regulates taxis, ride-hail, limousines, shuttles and inter-city buses in British Columbia.
note: Listed in the Ministry of Attorney General 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; not in the Transportation and Transit appendix and not on the tribunal-sector page. Inference: the tribunal-sector page names 19 AG tribunals, so PTB would make up TASD's stated 20.

name: Property Assessment Appeal Board
description: Second level of appeal for BC property assessments under the Assessment Act, after the Property Assessment Review Panels.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: Safety Standards Appeal Board
description: Adjudicative tribunal created under section 43 of the Safety Standards Act that hears appeals under that Act, the Homeowner Protection Act and the Building Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. The Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs 2026/27 service plan also lists it among that minister's organizations, so ministry-of-housing-and-municipal-affairs-2024 is an alternative parent.

name: Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board
description: Hears appeals under section 45 of the Skilled Trades BC Act about SkilledTradesBC decisions on trainees, authorizations and credentials.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: Surface Rights Board
description: Resolves disputes between landowners and companies that need access to private land to explore for or produce Crown-owned subsurface resources such as oil, gas, coal, minerals and geothermal.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

name: British Columbia Ferry Commission
description: Independent regulator under the Coastal Ferry Act that sets the price cap on fares for BC's coastal ferry operators and approves major capital expenditures.
note: Regulator, not a TASD tribunal. Listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; its website is titled 'Office of the BC Ferries Commissioner'.

name: Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal
description: Final level of appeal in BC's workers' compensation system, independent of WorkSafeBC, established under the Workers Compensation Act.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Labour (tribunal-sector page); also named in the Labour 2026/27 service plan.

name: Employment and Assistance Appeal Tribunal
description: Hears appeals of SDPR decisions on income and disability assistance, and of MCFD decisions under the Child Care Subsidy Act.
note: Administratively accountable to SDPR (tribunal-sector page); the Tribunal Chair reports to the Minister of SDPR (eaat.ca about page).

name: British Columbia Farm Industry Review Board
description: Supervises BC's regulated agricultural marketing boards and commissions and hears marketing, farm practices and BC SPCA animal custody appeals and complaints.
note: Created in 2003 by combining the BC Marketing Board (1934) and the Farm Practices Board (1997) (BCFIRB 'Learn about' page). Supervises the 8 marketing boards and commissions in the AF service plan, which are not recorded here.

name: Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch
description: Regulates licensing and permits for liquor and private cannabis retail establishments, manufacturers and events, and inspects licensees.
note: Agriculture and Food took responsibility in July 2025 (AF service plan). The PSSG service plan says oversight is shared with AF from July 17, 2025 and that compliance and enforcement stay with PSSG.

name: Independent Gambling Control Office
description: BC's gambling and horse-racing regulator under the Gaming Control Act, overseeing BCLC, charitable gaming and horse racing and administering Gambling Support BC.
note: Replaced the Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch (GPEB) on April 13, 2026. The Gaming Control Act was introduced by PSSG (news release 2025PSSG0067). The BCLC 2026/27 service plan still names GPEB in PSSG.

name: Disciplinary and Professional Conduct Board
description: Nine B.C. Teachers' Council members, appointed by the Minister, who hear teacher conduct and competence matters and certification appeals referred by the Commissioner for Teacher Regulation.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Education (tribunal-sector page).

name: Commissioner for Teacher Regulation
description: Independent statutory decision maker under the Teachers Act who oversees the discipline process for certified teachers in BC.
note: Regulatory office, not a tribunal. It is not in the Education 2026/27 service plan appendix, so the parent comes from its gov.bc.ca page location.

name: B.C. Teachers' Council
description: Sets standards under the Teachers Act for teachers' education, competence and professional conduct, and approves post-secondary teacher education programs.
note: Regulatory standards body listed in the Education 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

name: Health Care Practitioners Special Committee for Audit Hearings
description: Hears practitioners and decides whether the Medical Services Commission should recover payments after audits of health care practitioners.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Health (tribunal-sector page); acts under audit powers the Medical Services Commission delegated.

name: Medical Services Commission
description: Manages the Medical Services Plan under the Medicare Protection Act, ensuring reasonable access to medical care and managing payment for medical services.
note: Listed in the Health 2026/27 service plan Appendix A. The gov.bc.ca page URL tried returned 404.

name: Patient Care Quality Review Boards
description: Six independent review boards under the Patient Care Quality Review Board Act that review care complaints left unresolved by a health authority's Patient Care Quality Office.
note: Six boards shown as one dot.

name: Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board
description: Examines, registers and licenses BC emergency medical assistants, including first responders, under the Emergency Health Services Act.
note: Listed in the Health 2026/27 service plan Appendix A. The gov.bc.ca page URL tried returned 404.

name: Health Professions and Occupations Regulatory Oversight Office
description: Government-funded but independent office that audits and oversees the health regulatory colleges and houses a new independent discipline tribunal for serious misconduct hearings.
note: The release says the Province established it in 2024, led by Superintendent Sherri Young, and that its work began April 1, 2026 when the Health Professions and Occupations Act took effect. The discipline tribunal inside it has no separate record because the release gives it no proper name.

name: Property Assessment Review Panels
description: First level of appeal for BC property assessments under the Assessment Act, hearing owners' complaints each year from February 1 to March 15.
note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Finance (tribunal-sector page); listed in the Finance 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

name: Residential Tenancy Branch
description: Ministry branch that hears and resolves residential tenancy disputes between landlords and tenants.
note: A ministry branch rather than a statutory tribunal. The Housing 2026/27 service plan measures the share of RTB disputes heard within service standards.

name: Office of the BC Container Trucking Commissioner
description: Enforces the Container Trucking Act and issues Container Trucking Services licences for trucks serving Lower Mainland ports.
note: Established under the 2014 Container Trucking Act (OBCCTC site). Listed as 'BC Container Trucking Commission' in the Transportation 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

name: Managed Forest Council
description: Independent provincial agency under the Private Managed Forest Land Act that regulates forest practices on private managed forest land.
note: 'Established in May 2004' (MFC home page); listed in the Forests 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

name: BC Cancer
description: Leads the provincial planning and regional delivery of cancer care, from prevention and screening through treatment, survivorship and end-of-life care.

name: BC Centre for Disease Control
description: Provides provincial and national public health leadership through surveillance, detection, treatment, prevention and consultation services.

name: BC Children's Hospital and Sunny Hill Health Centre
description: BC's major treatment, teaching and research facilities for child health, caring for the most seriously ill or injured children in the province.

name: BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre
description: The only facility in B.C. devoted primarily to the health of women, newborns and families, and the only source of tertiary maternity care in the province.

name: BC Mental Health and Substance Use Services
description: Treats people with the most complex mental health and substance use needs referred by the regional health authorities or the courts.

name: BC Renal
description: Plans and coordinates the care of patients with kidney disease throughout the province.

name: BC Transplant
description: Responsible for all aspects of organ donation and transplantation in B.C.

name: Cardiac Services BC
description: Works to improve how cardiac services are managed and accessed throughout the province.

name: Perinatal Services BC
description: Provides leadership, support and coordination for the strategic planning of perinatal services and is the province's central source of perinatal information.

name: Provincial Laboratory Medicine Services
description: Administers laboratory services in B.C. and implements laboratory policies and processes on behalf of the Ministry of Health.

name: Trans Care BC
description: Provincial clinical program that sets direction and provides leadership for trans health services across B.C.

name: Health Emergency Management BC
description: Provides emergency management leadership and support to the B.C. health system, including the regional health authorities, PHSA and the Ministry of Health.

name: Powerex Corp.
description: Wholly owned energy marketing subsidiary of BC Hydro that trades wholesale power, natural gas and environmental products across North America.

name: Powertech Labs Inc.
description: Wholly owned BC Hydro subsidiary providing specialized testing and technical expertise to the energy sector, including hydrogen refuelling technology.
note: Service plan: incorporated 1988, originally established in Surrey in 1979.

name: BCHPA Captive Insurance Company Ltd.
description: Active BC Hydro subsidiary that procures insurance products and services on behalf of BC Hydro.

name: Columbia Hydro Constructors Ltd.
description: Active BC Hydro subsidiary that administers and supplies the labour force to specified projects.

name: Tongass Power and Light Company
description: Active BC Hydro subsidiary that supplies electricity to Hyder, Alaska from Stewart, B.C.

name: PlayNow
description: BCLC's regulated online gambling platform and the only legal option for online gambling in British Columbia.
note: Reported as the iGaming business segment in the service plan.

name: B.C. Lottotech International Inc.
description: Wholly owned BCLC subsidiary that buys capital assets and leases them to BCLC.

name: BC Builds
description: BC Housing-delivered program that uses low-cost financing, grants and underused land to build rental homes for middle-income households.
note: Announced February 13, 2024.

name: Licensing and Consumer Services
description: Administers the Homeowner Protection Act by licensing residential builders, requiring home warranty insurance on new homes, and handling enforcement and consumer information.
note: The 2026/27 service plan lists it as a separate BC Housing office.

name: Homeless Encampment Action Response Team and Temporary Housing
description: BC Housing initiatives (HEART and HEARTH) that respond to homeless encampments and provide temporary housing.

name: Building BC
description: BC Housing program for increasing the supply of housing, named alongside BC Builds in its 2026/27 service plan.

name: Arrow Lakes Power Corporation
description: Columbia Power subsidiary that owns the Arrow Lakes Generating Station and its 48-kilometre transmission line to BC Hydro's Selkirk Substation.
note: Boards have three directors each from Columbia Power and Columbia Basin Trust.

name: Brilliant Expansion Power Corporation
description: Columbia Power subsidiary that owns the Brilliant Expansion Generating Station.
note: Boards have three directors each from Columbia Power and Columbia Basin Trust.

name: Brilliant Power Corporation
description: Columbia Power subsidiary that owns the Brilliant Dam and the Brilliant Terminal Station.
note: Boards have three directors each from Columbia Power and Columbia Basin Trust.

name: Waneta Expansion Power Corporation
description: Columbia Power subsidiary that owns the 335 MW Waneta Expansion Generating Station.
note: Boards have three directors each from Columbia Power and Columbia Basin Trust. 335 MW figure from https://columbiapower.org/projects/.

name: Columbia Basin Broadband Corporation
description: Wholly owned Trust subsidiary building a region-wide fibre optic network to improve Basin connectivity.

name: FII Consulting (Shanghai) Co. Ltd.
description: Wholly owned FII subsidiary that develops the Chinese market for B.C. wood products.

name: FII Consulting India Private Limited
description: FII subsidiary that develops the Indian market for B.C. forest products.

name: Forestry Innovation Consulting (Vietnam) Ltd.
description: Wholly owned FII subsidiary that develops the Vietnamese market for B.C. forest products.

name: Vancouver Convention Centre
description: Convention facility operated by B.C. Pavilion Corporation.
note: Listed under Active Subsidiaries and Operating Segments in the PavCo service plan; it is an operating segment rather than a separate company.

name: BC Place
description: Stadium operated by B.C. Pavilion Corporation.
note: Listed as an operating segment in the PavCo service plan.

name: BC Renaissance Capital Fund
description: Wholly owned InBC subsidiary that manages legacy venture capital assets InBC inherited in 2020.

name: BCR Properties Ltd.
description: BCRC subsidiary that owns port-related lands leased to industrial tenants and terminal operators, including Vancouver Wharves and Squamish Terminals.

name: Pattullo Bridge Replacement Project
description: Bridge replacement project delivered by TI Corp for the Ministry of Transportation and Transit.
note: Listed as a current TI Corp project on its About page.

name: Broadway Subway Project
description: Major transit project delivered by TI Corp for the Ministry of Transportation and Transit.
note: Listed as a current TI Corp project on its About page.

name: Surrey Langley SkyTrain Project
description: Major transit project delivered by TI Corp for the Ministry of Transportation and Transit.
note: Listed as a current TI Corp project on its About page.

name: Fraser River Tunnel Project
description: Component of the Highway 99 Tunnel Program, delivered by TI Corp.
